translations.literal: On day Gengchen in the sixth month, the Great White transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: June, gengchen: Venus crossed the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 七月己卯，月犯太微，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On day Jimao in the seventh month, the moon transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure, and the Great White was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: July, jimao: the Moon crossed the enclosure while Venus shone by day.

sentences.zh: 自義熙元年至是，太白經天者九，日蝕者四，皆從上始，革代更王，臣失君之象也。

translations.literal: From the first Yixi year to this time, the Great White crossed the sky nine times; there were four solar eclipses; all began from above; these are images of dynastic change and replacement of kings, ministers losing their ruler.
translations.idiomatic: From Yixi one onward Venus transited the full heavens nine times and four eclipses began at the top—omens of usurpation, fallen kings, and ministers overpowering their sovereign.

translations.literal: That night, the Great White transgressed the Weeping star.
translations.idiomatic: That very night Venus crossed the Weeping star.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁巳，月、太白俱入羽林。

translations.literal: On day Dingsi in the twelfth month, the moon and the Great White both entered the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: December, dingsi: Moon and Venus entered the Feathered Forest together.

sentences.zh: 二年二月庚午，填星犯太微。

translations.literal: On day Gengwu in the second year’s second month, Saturn transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Year two, February, gengwu: Saturn crossed the Supreme Palace.

translations.literal: The prognostications were all the same as above.
translations.idiomatic: Same enclosure glosses repeated.

translations.literal: In the first year’s seventh month, Liu Yu received the title Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: First year, July: Liu Yu took the Song princedom.

translations.literal: In that year’s sixth month, the emperor abdicated in favor of Song.
translations.idiomatic: That June the emperor yielded the throne to Song.

translations.literal: Broom stars and guest stars
translations.idiomatic: Anomalous broom stars and guest stars

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年九月甲辰，客星見太微左掖門內。

translations.literal: In Wei Emperor Wen’s third Huangchu year, ninth month, day Jiachen, a guest star appeared inside the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s left Censor Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Huangchu three, ninth month, jiachen: a guest star shone inside the enclosure’s left rear gate.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「客星出太微，國有兵喪。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "When a guest star exits the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the state will have arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: A guest star leaving the enclosure foretells war and state funerals.

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the emperor campaigned south against Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: October: the emperor marched south against Sun Quan.

translations.literal: After this, there were repeated campaigns and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Endless conscription followed.

sentences.zh: 六年十月乙未，有星孛於少微，歷軒轅，占：「為兵喪，除舊布新之象。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, tenth month, day Yiwei, there was a broom star in Shao Wei; it passed through the Coachman; the prognostication: "It is arms and mourning; an image of removing the old and spreading the new."
translations.idiomatic: Year six, October, yiwei: a broom star blazed through Shao Wei and Xuanyuan; gloss—war, mourning, and regime renewal.

sentences.zh: 」時帝軍廣陵，辛丑，親御甲胃觀兵。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor’s army was at Guangling; on day Xinchou he personally donned armor and reviewed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The host lay at Guangling; on xinchou the sovereign inspected the troops in mail.

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Next year’s May: the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 明帝太和六年十一月丙寅，有星孛於翼，近太微上將星。

translations.literal: In Mingdi’s sixth Taihe year, eleventh month, day Bingyin, there was a broom star in the Wings, near the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s senior commander star.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi Taihe six, November, bingyin: a broom star appeared in the Wings beside the enclosure’s commander star.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: War and funerals are portended.

sentences.zh: 」甘氏曰：「孛彗所當之國，是受其殃。

translations.literal: Gan Shi states: "In whatever state a broom or comet strikes, that state receives its disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Shi warns that comets punish the realm they touch.

sentences.zh: 翼又楚分野，孫權封略也。

translations.literal: The Wings are also Chu’s field allotment, the territory Sun Quan enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The Wings mark Chu, Sun Quan’s domain.

translations.literal: The next year, Quan suffered defeat in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Sun Quan met disaster in Liaodong.

translations.literal: The year after that, Zhuge Liang entered the Qin riverlands.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhuge Liang advanced into the Qin valleys.

sentences.zh: 孫權發兵，緣江淮屯要衝，權自圍新城以應亮，天子東征權。

translations.literal: Sun Quan raised troops, along the Yangzi and Huai garrisoned the choke points; Quan himself besieged Xincheng in answer to Liang; the Son of Heaven campaigned east against Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan mobilized along the Yangzi and Huai, personally besieged Xincheng to aid Zhuge Liang, while the Wei emperor marched east against him.

sentences.zh: 青龍四年十月甲申，有星孛於大辰，長三尺。

translations.literal: In the fourth Qinglong year, tenth month, day Jiashen, there was a broom star at the Great Chen, three feet long.
translations.idiomatic: Qinglong four, October, jiashen: a three-foot broom star appeared at the Great Chen.

translations.literal: On day Yiyou, there was again a broom in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyou: another eastern broom star.

sentences.zh: 十一月己亥，彗星見，犯宦者天紀星。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, day Jihai, a comet appeared, transgressing the eunuch and Celestial Tally stars.
translations.idiomatic: November, jihai: a comet crossed the eunuch and Celestial Tally stars.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「大辰為天王，天下有喪。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The Great Chen is the Celestial King; under Heaven there will be mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The Great Chen is the royal seat; the realm faces mourning.

sentences.zh: 」劉向《五紀論》曰：「《春秋》，星孛於東方，不言宿者，不加宿也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang’s "Treatise on the Five Eras" states: "In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a star broomed the east and no lodge was named, it means a lodge was not added."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang’s Five Eras treatise notes that unnamed eastern comets omit explicit lodge tags.

sentences.zh: 宦者在天市，為中外有兵。

translations.literal: Eunuchs are in the Celestial Market; it means inner and outer will have arms.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch stars sit in the Celestial Market, signaling war inside and out.

sentences.zh: 天紀為地震，孛彗主兵喪。

translations.literal: The Celestial Tally means earthquake; brooms and comets govern arms and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Tally star signals earthquakes; comets and brooms still mean war and mourning.

translations.literal: In the first Jingchu year’s sixth month, there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu one, June: an earthquake struck.

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wu general Zhu Ran besieged Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: September: Wu’s Zhu Ran ringed Jiangxia.

translations.literal: Empress Mao died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Mao passed away.

translations.literal: In the second year’s first month, they campaigned against Gongsun Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Year two, first month: expedition against Gongsun Wenyi.

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month, Mingdi died.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, first month: Emperor Ming died.

sentences.zh: 景初二年八月，彗星見張，長三尺，逆西行，四十一日滅。

translations.literal: In Jingchu second year, eighth month, a comet appeared in Zhang, three feet long, moving retrograde west, and was extinguished after forty-one days.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchu two, August: a three-foot comet in Zhang moved west retrograde and vanished after forty-one days.

translations.literal: The prognostication was the same as above.
translations.idiomatic: Same comet gloss as prior entries.

translations.literal: Zhang is the field allotment of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang marks the Zhou celestial field.

sentences.zh: 十月癸巳，客星見危，逆行，在離宮北、騰蛇南。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, day Guisi, a guest star appeared in Rooftops, moving retrograde, north of the Detached Palace and south of Coiled Serpent.
translations.idiomatic: October, guisi: a guest star shone in Rooftops, retrograde between the Detached Palace and Coiled Serpent.

translations.literal: On day Jiachen, it transgressed the Ancestral star.
translations.idiomatic: Jiachen: it crossed the Ancestral star.

translations.literal: On day Jiyou, it was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyou: it vanished.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Wherever a guest star appears there will be arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Guest stars bring war and death to their station.

translations.literal: Emptiness and Rooftops are the ancestral temple; they are also tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Void and Rooftops mark the dynastic shrine and burial ground.

sentences.zh: 客星近離宮，則宮中將有大喪，就先君於宗廟之象也。

translations.literal: A guest star near the Detached Palace means the palace will soon have great mourning, an image of joining the former lords in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Near the Detached Palace it foretells deep palace mourning, as though the ruler were joining his ancestors.

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, first month: the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 少帝正始元年十月乙酉，彗星見西方，在尾，長三丈，拂牽牛，犯太白。

translations.literal: In the Young Emperor’s first Zhengshi year, tenth month, day Yiyou, a comet appeared in the west, in the Tail, three rods long, brushing the Oxherd and transgressing the Great White.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengshi one, October, yiyou: a western comet in the Tail, three rods long, swept the Oxherd and crossed Venus.

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, day Jiazi, it advanced and transgressed the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: November, jiazi: the comet advanced into the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「尾為燕，又為吳，牛亦吳越之分。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The Tail is Yan and also Wu; the Ox is also Wu and Yue’s division."
translations.idiomatic: The Tail marks Yan and Wu; the Ox marks Wu-Yue.

sentences.zh: 太白為上將，羽林中軍兵。

translations.literal: The Great White is the senior commander; the Feathered Forest is central-army troops.
translations.idiomatic: Venus is the commander star; the Feathered Forest is palace guards.

translations.literal: It means Wu and Yue will have mourning and central-army troops will move.
translations.idiomatic: Wu-Yue face funerals while household regiments stir.

translations.literal: In the second year’s fifth month, Wu dispatched three generals to raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: Year two, May: Wu sent three generals to strike the frontier.

translations.literal: Wu heir Deng died.
translations.idiomatic: Wu crown prince Sun Deng died.

sentences.zh: 六月，宣帝討諸葛恪於皖。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the August Lord campaigned against Zhuge Ke at Wan.
translations.idiomatic: June: Sima Yi attacked Zhuge Ke at Wan.

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Man Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Man Chong passed away.

sentences.zh: 六年八月戊午，彗星見七星，長二尺，色白，進至張，積二十三日滅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, eighth month, day Wuwu, a comet appeared at the Seven Stars, two feet long, white in color, advanced to Zhang, and was extinguished after twenty-three days.
translations.idiomatic: Year six, August, wuwu: a white two-foot comet moved from the Seven Stars to Zhang and vanished in twenty-three days.

sentences.zh: 七年十一月癸亥，又見軫，長一尺，積百五十六日滅。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, eleventh month, day Guihai, it again appeared in the Chariot, one foot long, and was extinguished after one hundred fifty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: Year seven, November, guihai: another comet in the Chariot lasted one hundred fifty-six days.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，又見昴，長六尺，色青白，芒西南指。

translations.literal: In the ninth year’s third month, it again appeared in the Hairy Head, six feet long, bluish white, its ray pointing southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Year nine, March: a six-foot bluish-white comet in the Pleiades aimed its tail southwest.

sentences.zh: 七月，又見翼，長二尺，進至軫，積四十二日滅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, it again appeared in the Wings, two feet long, advanced to the Chariot, and was extinguished after forty-two days.
translations.idiomatic: July: a two-foot comet in the Wings crept to the Chariot and died out in forty-two days.

sentences.zh: 案占曰：「七星張為周分野，翼軫為楚，昴為趙魏。

translations.literal: Investigating, the prognostication states: "The Seven Stars and Zhang are Zhou’s field allotment; Wings and Chariot are Chu; the Hairy Head is Zhao and Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary maps the Seven Stars and Zhang to Zhou, Wings and Chariot to Chu, and the Pleiades to Zhao-Wei.

sentences.zh: 彗所以除舊布新，主兵喪也。

translations.literal: Comets thereby remove the old and spread the new; they govern arms and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Comets scour away the old order and foretell war and death.

sentences.zh: 」嘉平元年，宣帝誅曹爽兄弟及其党與，皆夷三族，京師嚴兵。

translations.literal: In the first Jiaping year, the August Lord executed Cao Shuang and his younger brothers and their partisans, all exterminating three clans; the capital was under strict arms.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaping one: Sima Yi slew Cao Shuang’s faction to the third degree and locked down Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 三年，誅楚王彪，又襲王淩於淮南。

translations.literal: In the third year, he executed the Prince of Chu, Biao, and also struck Wang Ling in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Year three: Prince Biao of Chu died and Wang Ling was crushed in Huainan.

translations.literal: Huainan is eastern Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan counts as eastern Chu territory.

translations.literal: Wei’s princes were confined at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei imperial princes were imprisoned at Ye.

sentences.zh: 嘉平三年十一月癸亥，有星孛于營室，西行，積九十日滅。

translations.literal: In Jiaping third year, eleventh month, day Guihai, there was a broom star in Encampment, moving west, extinguished after ninety days.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaping three, November, guihai: a ninety-day western broom star in Encampment.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "There will be arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: War and funerals follow.

translations.literal: Encampment is the rear palace; the rear palace will moreover have disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Encampment marks the harem, which now faces turmoil.

sentences.zh: 」四年二月丁酉，彗星見西方，在胃，長五六丈，色白，芒南指，貫參，積二十日滅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, second month, day Dingyou, a comet appeared in the west, in the Stomach, five or six rods long, white in color, its ray pointing south, piercing Orion, extinguished after twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: Year four, February, dingyou: a huge white western comet in the Stomach pierced Orion and faded in twenty days.

sentences.zh: 五年十一月，彗星又見軫，長五丈，在太微左執法西，東南指，積百九十日滅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year’s eleventh month, a comet again appeared in the Chariot, five rods long, west of the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s Left Law Enforcer, pointing southeast, extinguished after one hundred ninety days.
translations.idiomatic: Year five, November: a five-rod comet in the Chariot west of the Left Law Enforcer lingered one hundred ninety days.

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: "The Stomach is Yan Province’s field allotment."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary ties the Stomach to Yanzhou.

translations.literal: Orion governs arms.
translations.idiomatic: Orion’s Belt stars govern warfare.

translations.literal: The Supreme Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven’s court.
translations.idiomatic: The enclosure is the celestial court of the sovereign.

translations.literal: The Law Enforcer is the wielder of government.
translations.idiomatic: Law Enforcer stars mark chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 孛彗為兵喪，除舊布新之象。

translations.literal: Brooms and comets are images of arms and mourning, removing the old and spreading the new.
translations.idiomatic: Comets signal war, death, and dynastic turnover.

sentences.zh: 」正元元年二月，李豐、豐弟翼、後父張緝等謀亂，皆誅，皇后亦廢。

translations.literal: In the first Zhengyuan year’s second month, Li Feng, Feng’s younger brother Yi, the empress’s father Zhang Ji, and others plotted rebellion; all were executed; the empress was also deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyuan one, February: Li Feng, Li Yi, Zhang Ji, and co. fell to execution and the empress was cast down.

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the emperor was deposed and made Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: September: the emperor was demoted to Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公正元元年十一月，白氣出南斗側，廣數丈，長竟天。

translations.literal: In the first Zhengyuan year of the Duke of Gaoxiang Township, eleventh month, white vapor issued beside the Southern Dipper, several rods wide, its length spanning the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoxiang Duke Zhengyuan one, November: white qi flared beside the Dipper, yards wide and sky-long.

sentences.zh: 王肅曰：「蚩尤之旗也，東南其有亂乎！

translations.literal: Wang Su states: "It is the banner of Chiyou; will the southeast have turmoil?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su calls it Chiyou’s war-banner and asks if the southeast will riot.

sentences.zh: 」二年正月，有彗星見於吳楚分，西北竟天。

translations.literal: In the second year’s first month, there was a comet seen in Wu and Chu’s division, stretching northwest across the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Year two, first month: a comet filled the Wu-Chu sector northwestward.

sentences.zh: 鎮東大將軍毋丘儉等據淮南叛，景帝討平之。

translations.literal: Eastern-stabilizing Grand General Wuqiu Jian and others held Huainan in rebellion; the Brilliant Emperor campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuqiu Jian seized Huainan until Sima Shi crushed the revolt.

sentences.zh: 案占：「蚩尤旗見，王者征伐四方。

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: "When Chiyou’s banner appears, the king campaigns in the four directions."
translations.idiomatic: The Chiyou-banner gloss means the sovereign sends armies everywhere.

translations.literal: Afterward he again campaigned against Huainan and pacified Ba and Shu in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Later campaigns hit Huainan again and subdued Ba-Shu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，吳主孫亮五鳳元年也。

translations.literal: That year was also Wu ruler Sun Liang’s first Wufeng year.
translations.idiomatic: The same year was Sun Liang of Wu’s Wufeng era.

translations.literal: Dipper and Ox are Wu and Yue’s division.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper-Ox zone marks Wu-Yue.

sentences.zh: 案占：「吳有兵喪，除舊布新之象也。

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: "Wu will have arms and mourning; it is an image of removing the old and spreading the new."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary says Wu faces war and renewal.

sentences.zh: 」太平三年，孫綝盛兵圍宮，廢亮為會稽王，故《國志》又書于吳也。

translations.literal: In the third Taiping year, Sun Chen massed troops and surrounded the palace, deposing Liang as Prince of Kuaiji; therefore the "National Records" also records it under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping three: Sun Chen besieged the palace, demoted Sun Liang to Prince of Kuaiji, so the chronicle logs it for Wu too.

sentences.zh: 淮南江東同揚州地，故于時變見吳、楚。

translations.literal: Huainan and Jiangdong share Yangzhou ground; therefore at that time the anomaly appeared in Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan and Jiangdong both lie in Yangzhou, so the sign showed in Wu-Chu.

sentences.zh: 楚之分則魏之淮南，多與吳同災。

translations.literal: Chu’s division in Wei is Huainan, which mostly shares calamities with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s Huainan sector mirrors Wu’s omens.

sentences.zh: 是以毋丘儉以孛為己應，遂起兵而敗。

translations.literal: Therefore Wuqiu Jian took the comet as answering to himself, thereupon raised troops and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wuqiu Jian read the comet as his own sign, rose anyway, and lost.

sentences.zh: 後三年，即魏甘露二年，諸葛誕又反淮南，吳遣將救之。

translations.literal: Three years later, that is Wei’s second Ganlu year, Zhuge Dan again rebelled in Huainan; Wu sent generals to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Three years on, Ganlu two: Zhuge Dan rebelled in Huainan with Wu relief columns.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，誕眾與吳兵死沒各數萬人，猶前長星之應也。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Dan’s host and Wu’s troops each died or drowned in the tens of thousands, still matching the earlier long comet.
translations.idiomatic: At the fall tens of thousands of Dan’s and Wu’s soldiers perished—fulfilling the long-comet omen.

sentences.zh: 甘露二年十一月，彗星見角，色白。

translations.literal: In Ganlu second year, eleventh month, a comet appeared in the Horn, white in color.
translations.idiomatic: Ganlu two, November: a white comet in the Horn.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「彗星見兩角間色白者，軍起不戰，邦有大喪。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "When a comet appears between the two Horns and is white, armies rise without battle and the state has great mourning."
translations.idiomatic: A white comet between the Horns means armies mass without fighting and the dynasty mourns deeply.

sentences.zh: 」景元元年，高貴鄉公為成濟所害。

translations.literal: In the first Jingyuan year, the Duke of Gaoxiang Township was killed by Cheng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan one: Cao Mao fell to Cheng Ji’s blade.

sentences.zh: 四年十月丁丑，客星見太微中，轉東南行，歷軫宿，積七日滅。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, tenth month, day Dingchou, a guest star appeared inside the Supreme Palace Enclosure, turned moving southeast, passed through the Chariot station, and was extinguished after seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Year four, October, dingchou: a week-long guest star drifted through the enclosure toward the Chariot.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「客星出太微，有兵喪。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "When a guest star exits the Supreme Palace Enclosure, there will be arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Guest stars leaving the enclosure mean war and death.

translations.literal: In the first Jingyuan year, the Duke of Gaoxiang Township was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan one repeated Cao Mao’s assassination.

sentences.zh: 元帝景元三年十一月壬寅，彗星見亢，色白，長五寸，轉北行，積四十五日滅。

translations.literal: In Yuan Di’s third Jingyuan year, eleventh month, day Renyin, a comet appeared in the Neck, white in color, five inches long, turned moving north, extinguished after forty-five days.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor Yuan, Jingyuan three, November, renyin: a five-inch white comet in the Neck moved north forty-five days.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: War and funerals again.

translations.literal: One gloss says: "When a comet appears in the Neck, the Son of Heaven loses virtue."
translations.idiomatic: A variant warns the ruler loses moral mandate.

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Zhong Hui and Deng Ai campaigned against Shu and conquered it.
translations.idiomatic: Year four: Zhong Hui and Deng Ai took Shu.

translations.literal: The two generals rebelled and were disorderly; both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Both generals mutinied and died under sentence.

sentences.zh: 咸熙二年五月，彗星見王良，長丈餘，色白，東南指，積十二日滅。

translations.literal: In the second Xianxi year, fifth month, a comet appeared at Wang Liang, more than a rod long, white in color, pointing southeast, extinguished after twelve days.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxi two, May: a white, yard-long comet at Wang Liang pointed southeast twelve days.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Wang Liang is the Son of Heaven’s chariot-team."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang marks the royal charioteer stars.

sentences.zh: 彗星掃之，禪代之表，除舊布新之象也。

translations.literal: A comet sweeping it is a sign of abdication in favor of another, an image of removing the old and spreading the new.
translations.idiomatic: A comet brushing Wang Liang foretells abdication and regime change.

translations.literal: White color means mourning.
translations.idiomatic: White comets add mourning.

sentences.zh: 王良在東壁宿，又并州之分野。

translations.literal: Wang Liang is in the eastern Wall lodge; it is also Bing Province’s field allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang sits in Wall and ties to Bingzhou’s celestial field.

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Emperor Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: August: King Wen (Sima Zhao) died, clearing the way for usurpation.

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Emperor Wu received Wei’s abdication.
translations.idiomatic: December: Sima Yan accepted Wei’s abdication.

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始四年正月丙戌，彗星見軫，青白色，西北行，又轉東行。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu’s fourth Taishi year, first month, day Bingxu, a comet appeared in the Chariot, greenish white, moving northwest, then turning east.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Taishi four, first month, bingxu: a green-white comet in the Chariot drifted northwest then east.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「為兵喪，軫又楚分野。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning; the Chariot is also Chu’s field allotment."
translations.idiomatic: War and death, with Chu’s field implicated.

translations.literal: In the third month, Empress Dowager Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: March: Empress Dowager Wang passed away.

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Wu raided Jiangxia and Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: October: Wu struck Jiangxia and Xiangyang.

translations.literal: In the fifth year’s ninth month, a star broomed the Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Year five, September: a broom star swept the Purple Palace.

translations.literal: The prognostication was as above.
translations.idiomatic: The usual Purple Palace gloss applied.

translations.literal: The Purple Palace is the Son of Heaven’s inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Purple Palace is the celestial inner court.

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Empress Yang the Martial Origin died.
translations.idiomatic: Year ten: Empress Yang Wu yuan died.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月，有星孛於軫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year’s twelfth month, there was a star brooming in the Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Year ten, December: a broom star in the Chariot.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天下兵起，軫又楚分野。」

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Under Heaven arms will arise; the Chariot is also Chu’s field allotment."
translations.idiomatic: Realm-wide war looms; the Chariot again marks Chu.

sentences.zh: 咸寧二年六月甲戌，星孛於氐。

translations.literal: In the second Xianning year, sixth month, day Jiaxu, a star broomed in the Root.
translations.idiomatic: Xianning two, June, jiaxu: a broom star in the Root.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The Son of Heaven loses virtue and changes governance."
translations.idiomatic: The throne loses virtue and shifts policy.

translations.literal: The Root is also Yan Province’s division.
translations.idiomatic: The Root also maps to Yanzhou.

translations.literal: In the seventh month, a star broomed the Great Horn.
translations.idiomatic: July: a broom star swept Arcturus.

translations.literal: The Great Horn is the emperor’s seat.
translations.idiomatic: Arcturus is the celestial throne.

sentences.zh: 八月，星孛太微，至翼、北斗、三台。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, a star broomed the Supreme Palace Enclosure, reaching the Wings, Northern Dipper, and Three Steps.
translations.idiomatic: August: a broom ran through the enclosure to Wings, the Dipper, and Three Steps.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「太微，天子庭，大人惡之。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The Supreme Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven’s court; great men find it ominous."
translations.idiomatic: The enclosure warns great lords of ill omen.

translations.literal: One gloss says: "There will be change of king."
translations.idiomatic: A variant predicts a new king.

translations.literal: The Wings are also Chu’s field allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Wings again mark Chu.

sentences.zh: 北斗主殺罰，三台為三公。

translations.literal: The Northern Dipper governs killing and punishment; the Three Steps are the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper rules executions; the Three Steps are the three dukes.

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month, a star broomed in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Year three, first month: a western broom star.

translations.literal: In the third month, a star broomed in the Stomach.
translations.idiomatic: March: a broom in the Stomach.

translations.literal: The Stomach is Xu Province’s division.
translations.idiomatic: The Stomach maps to Xuzhou.

translations.literal: In the fourth month, a star broomed the Woman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: April: a broom crossed the Woman Attendant stars.

translations.literal: The Woman Attendant is the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Those stars mark the harem.

translations.literal: In the fifth month, it again broomed in the east.
translations.idiomatic: May: another eastern broom.

translations.literal: In the seventh month, a star broomed the Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: July: a broom swept the Purple Palace.

translations.literal: The superior gloss states: "Under Heaven the ruler will change."
translations.idiomatic: High commentary reads: the throne changes hands.

translations.literal: In the fourth year’s fourth month, Chiyou’s banner appeared in the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: Year four, April: Chiyou’s banner showed in the Eastern Well.

sentences.zh: 後二年，傾三方伐吳，是其應也。

translations.literal: After two years the dynasty tilted three fronts to campaign against Wu; this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the tripartite assault on Wu matched the sign.

translations.literal: In the fifth year’s third month, a star broomed in the Willow.
translations.idiomatic: Year five, March: a broom in the Willow.

translations.literal: In the fourth month, it again broomed in the Woman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: April: another sweep of the Woman Attendant.

translations.literal: In the seventh month, it broomed in the Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: July: the Purple Palace was broomed again.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Outer ministers encroach on the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Border ministers bully the throne.

translations.literal: The Willow is also the Three Rivers’ field allotment.
translations.idiomatic: The Willow marks the Three Rivers zone.

sentences.zh: 大角、太微、紫宮、女御並為王者。

translations.literal: The Great Horn, Supreme Palace Enclosure, Purple Palace, and Woman Attendant all stand for the king.
translations.idiomatic: Arcturus, the enclosure, Purple Palace, and Woman Attendant all image the sovereign.

translations.literal: The next year Wu perished; this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Wu fell—exactly as foretold.

translations.literal: Brooming governs arms and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Broom stars mean war and death.

sentences.zh: 征吳之役，三河、徐、兗之兵悉出，交戰于吳楚之地，吳丞相都督以下梟戮十數，偏裨行陣之徒馘斬萬計，皆其徵也。

translations.literal: In the Wu campaign, the hosts of the Three Rivers, Xu, and Yan all marched out, battling in Wu-Chu lands; Wu’s chancellor and area commanders down were beheaded by the dozen, while subordinate officers and rank-and-file lost heads by the myriad—all were its signs.
translations.idiomatic: The conquest of Wu threw Three Rivers, Xu, and Yan armies into Wu-Chu fighting, beheading Wu’s command stack by the dozen and common soldiers by the myriad—each tally matched the omens.

sentences.zh: 太康二年八月，有星孛于張。

translations.literal: In the second Taikang year’s eighth month, a star broomed in Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang two, August: a broom star in Zhang.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning follow.

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, a star broomed at the Coachman’s yoke-stars.
translations.idiomatic: In November a comet swept across the Coachman’s yoke stars in the eastern sky.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The rear palace will answer for it."
translations.idiomatic: The harem bears the omen.

translations.literal: In the fourth year’s third month, day Wushen, a star broomed in the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Year four, March, wushen: a broom star in the southwest.

sentences.zh: 是年，齊王攸、任城王陵、琅邪王伷、新都王該薨。

translations.literal: That year, Prince You of Qi, Prince Ling of Rencheng, Prince Xiu of Langye, and Prince Gai of Xindu died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Princes You, Ling, Xiu, and Gai died.

sentences.zh: 八年九月，星孛於南斗，長數十丈餘日滅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year’s ninth month, a star broomed at the Southern Dipper, several tens of rods long, extinguished after many days.
translations.idiomatic: Year eight, September: a vast broom star on the Dipper lasted many days.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「斗主爵祿，國有大憂。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The Dipper governs noble rank and stipend; the state will have great grief."
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper ties to offices and stipends; the realm faces deep sorrow.

sentences.zh: 」一曰：「孛于斗，王者疾病，天下易政，大亂兵起。」

translations.literal: One gloss says: "When it brooms the Dipper, the king will be ill, under Heaven governance will change, and great disorder and arms will arise."
translations.idiomatic: A variant adds royal illness, political overturn, and massive war.

sentences.zh: 太熙元年四月，客星在紫宮。

translations.literal: In the first Taixi year’s fourth month, a guest star was in the Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Taixi one, April: a guest star shone in the Purple Palace.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: War and death follow.

translations.literal: Near the end of Taikang, Emperor Wu indulged feasts and outings and had many illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Late Taikang saw Emperor Wu lost in revels and sickness.

translations.literal: In that month, day Jiyou, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That month, jiyou: the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 永平元年，賈后誅楊駿及其黨與，皆夷三族，楊太后亦見弑。

translations.literal: In the first Yongping year, Empress Jia executed Yang Jun and his partisans, all exterminating three clans; Empress Dowager Yang was also murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping one: Empress Jia wiped out Yang Jun’s faction to the third degree and killed Empress Dowager Yang.

sentences.zh: 又誅汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋，王室兵喪之應也。

translations.literal: She also executed Prince Liang of Runan, Grand Guardian Wei Guan, and Prince Wei of Chu—responses to royal-house arms and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: She also killed Princes Liang and Wei and Grand Guardian Wei Guan—royal bloodletting matching the omens.

sentences.zh: 惠帝元康五年四月，有星孛於奎，至軒轅、太微，經三台、太陵。

translations.literal: In Emperor Hui’s fifth Yuankang year, fourth month, there was a star brooming in the Strider, reaching the Coachman and Supreme Palace Enclosure, passing the Three Steps and Great Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang five, April: a broom star ran from Kui through Xuanyuan and the enclosure across Three Steps and Great Tomb.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「奎為魯，又為庫兵，軒轅為後宮，太微天子庭，三台為三司，太陵有積尸死喪之事。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The Strider is Lu and also armory troops; the Coachman is the rear palace; the Supreme Palace Enclosure is the Son of Heaven’s court; the Three Steps are the three ministers; the Great Tomb has piled corpses and death-mourning affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Kui marks Lu and arsenals; Xuanyuan the harem; the enclosure the court; Three Steps the ministers; Great Tomb mass death.

translations.literal: Afterward the armory burned and the western Qiang rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Then the arsenal caught fire and western Qiang rose.

sentences.zh: 後五年，司空張華遇禍，賈后廢死，魯公賈謐誅。

translations.literal: After five years, Minister of Works Zhang Hua met disaster; Empress Jia was deposed and died; Duke Lu Jia Mi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Five years on: Zhang Hua perished, Empress Jia fell, and Jia Mi died.

translations.literal: The next year, Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Prince Zhao Lun seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是三王興兵討倫，兵士戰死十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three princes raised arms against Lun; soldiers who died in battle exceeded one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Three princes marched on Lun and left a hundred thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 永康元年三月，妖星見南方。

translations.literal: In the first Yongkang year’s third month, an uncanny star appeared in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Yongkang one, March: a freak southern star.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「妖星出，天下大兵將起。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "When an uncanny star appears, under Heaven great arms will arise."
translations.idiomatic: Uncanny stars herald realm-wide war.

sentences.zh: 」是月賈后殺太子，趙王倫尋廢殺后，斬司空張華，又廢帝自立。

translations.literal: That month Empress Jia killed the heir; Prince Zhao Lun soon deposed and killed the empress, beheaded Minister of Works Zhang Hua, and also deposed the emperor and set himself up.
translations.idiomatic: That month Empress Jia murdered the crown prince; Lun then killed her and Zhang Hua, deposed the emperor, and seized power.

sentences.zh: 於是三王並起，迭總天權。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three princes all rose, passing the supreme mandate in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Three princes rose in rotation, each holding the reins.

sentences.zh: 其十二月，彗星出牽牛之西，指天市。

translations.literal: That twelfth month, a comet issued west of the Oxherd, pointing at the Celestial Market.
translations.idiomatic: That December a comet sprang west of the Oxherd toward the Celestial Market.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「牛者七政始，彗出之，改元易號之象也。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The Ox is the beginning of the seven regulators; when a comet issues from it, it is an image of changing era-name and altering reign-title."
translations.idiomatic: The Ox opens the seven celestial powers; a comet there means new era names.

sentences.zh: 天市一名天府，一名天子旗，帝坐在其中。

translations.literal: The Celestial Market is also called the Celestial Treasury and also called the Son of Heaven’s banner; the emperor’s seat lies within it.
translations.idiomatic: The Market is heaven’s treasury, the royal banner, with the throne inside.

sentences.zh: 」明年，趙王倫篡位，改元，尋為大兵所滅。

translations.literal: The next year, Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne, changed the era-name, and soon was destroyed by a great army.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Lun seized power, changed the era, then fell to a great host.

translations.literal: In the second year’s fourth month, a comet appeared in Qi’s division.
translations.idiomatic: Year two, April: a comet in Qi’s sector.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Qi will have arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Qi faces war and death.

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Qi, Jiong, raised troops to campaign against Prince Zhao Lun.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiong of Qi marched against Zhao Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫滅，冏擁兵不朝，專權淫奢。

translations.literal: When Lun was destroyed, Jiong held troops and did not attend court, monopolizing power, dissolute and extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun fell, Jiong kept armies private, skipped court, and ruled licentiously.

translations.literal: The next year, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jiong was executed.

sentences.zh: 太安元年四月，彗星晝見。

translations.literal: In the first Tai’an year’s fourth month, a comet was seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: Tai’an one, April: a daylight comet.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，彗星見東方，指三台。

translations.literal: In the second year’s third month, a comet appeared in the east, pointing at the Three Steps.
translations.idiomatic: Year two, March: an eastern comet aimed at the Three Steps.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is an image of arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning are imaged.

translations.literal: The Three Steps are the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Three Steps mark the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 」三年正月，東海王越執太尉、長沙王乂，張方又殺之。

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month, Prince of the Eastern Sea, Yue, seized Grand Commandant and Prince of Changsha, Yi, and Zhang Fang also killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Year three, first month: Sima Yue arrested Sima Yi; Zhang Fang then killed him.

sentences.zh: 永興元年五月，客星守畢。

translations.literal: In the first Yongxing year’s fifth month, a guest star guarded the Net.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing one, May: a guest star stationed at the Net.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The Son of Heaven will cut off heirs."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial line risks extinction.

translations.literal: One gloss says: "Great ministers will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: A variant cites ministerial executions.

sentences.zh: 」時諸王擁兵，其後惠帝失統，終無繼嗣。

translations.literal: At the time the various princes held troops; afterward Emperor Hui lost the thread of rule and ultimately had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: Princely armies ruled; Hui never secured an heir.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，有星孛于昴畢。

translations.literal: In the second year’s eighth month, there was a star brooming in the Hairy Head and Net.
translations.idiomatic: Year two, August: a broom through Pleiades and Net.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: War and death again.

translations.literal: The Hairy Head and Net are also Zhao and Wei’s field allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Pleiades-Net map to Zhao-Wei.

translations.literal: On day Dingchou in the tenth month, there was a star brooming at the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: October, dingchou: a broom on the Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「琁璣更授，天子出走。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The pearl pivots change hands; the Son of Heaven flees."
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper’s mandate shifts; the emperor runs.

translations.literal: It also says: "A strong state will raise arms; feudal lords will contend for power."
translations.idiomatic: Another line warns of hegemons and baronial strife.

translations.literal: Afterward the various princes crossed arms; each had a response.
translations.idiomatic: Princes then tore at one another, each omen fulfilled.

translations.literal: The next year, Emperor Hui died.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Emperor Hui died.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸和四年七月，有星孛於西北，犯斗，二十三日滅。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng’s fourth Xianhe year, seventh month, there was a star brooming in the northwest, transgressing the Dipper, extinguished after twenty-three days.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe four, July: a northwestern broom crossed the Dipper and died in twenty-three days.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is military turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: Mutiny is portended.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，郭默殺江州刺史劉胤，荊州刺史陶侃討默，斬之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Guo Mo killed Inspector of Jiang Province Liu Yin; Inspector of Jing Province Tao Kan campaigned against Mo and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: December: Guo Mo slew Liu Yin; Tao Kan took his head.

translations.literal: At the time Shi Le also first assumed a usurped title.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le too began usurping royal styles.

sentences.zh: 咸康二年正月辛巳，彗星夕見西方，在奎。

translations.literal: In the second Xiankang year, first month, day Xinsi, a comet was seen at evening in the west, in the Strider.
translations.idiomatic: Xiankang two, first month, xinsi: an evening comet in the Strider.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning.

translations.literal: The Strider is also border troops.
translations.idiomatic: Kui also signals frontier armies.

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month, Shi Jilong usurped the title Celestial King.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, first month: Shi Hu took the Celestial King title.

sentences.zh: 四年，石季龍伐慕容皝，不克。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Shi Jilong campaigned against Murong Huang and did not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Year four: Shi Hu attacked Murong Huang without success.

sentences.zh: 既退，皝追擊之，又破麻秋。

translations.literal: When he withdrew, Huang pursued and struck him, and again defeated Ma Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: On retreat Murong Huang chased him and broke Ma Qiu too.

translations.literal: At the time Huang declared himself a vassal; it matched border troops.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang’s submission matched the border-troop omen.

sentences.zh: 六年二月庚辰，有星孛於太微。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, second month, day Gengchen, there was a star brooming in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Year six, February, gengchen: a broom in the Supreme Palace.

translations.literal: In the seventh year’s third month, Empress Du died.
translations.idiomatic: Year seven, March: Empress Du died.

sentences.zh: 康帝建元元年十一月六日，彗星見亢，長七尺，白色。

translations.literal: In Emperor Kang’s first Jianyuan year, eleventh month, sixth day, a comet appeared in the Neck, seven feet long, white.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyuan one, eleventh month, sixth day: a seven-foot white comet in the Neck.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The Neck is the court; it governs arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The Neck marks the court and its wars and funerals.

translations.literal: In the second year, Emperor Kang died.
translations.idiomatic: Year two: Emperor Kang died.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和五年十一月乙卯，彗星見於亢。

translations.literal: In Emperor Mu’s fifth Yonghe year, eleventh month, day Yimao, a comet appeared in the Neck.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe five, November, yimao: a comet in the Neck.

translations.literal: Its ray pointed west, white in color, one rod long.
translations.idiomatic: Its tail aimed west, white, one rod long.

sentences.zh: 六年正月丁丑，彗星又見於亢。

translations.literal: On day Dingchou in the sixth year’s first month, a comet again appeared in the Neck.
translations.idiomatic: Year six, first month, dingchou: another Neck comet.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning, pestilence."
translations.idiomatic: War, mourning, and plague.

translations.literal: In that year’s fifth month, eighth month, Chu Pou’s northern expedition was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: That year’s August: Chu Pou’s northern campaign failed.

sentences.zh: 十一月，冉閔殺石遵，又盡殺胡十餘萬人，於是中土大亂。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Ran Min killed Shi Zun and also slaughtered more than one hundred thousand Hu; thereupon the central plain was greatly chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: November: Ran Min slew Shi Zun and massacred a hundred thousand Hu, throwing the heartland into chaos.

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Chu Pou died.
translations.idiomatic: December: Chu Pou died.

translations.literal: That year, great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought a great epidemic.

sentences.zh: 升平二年五月丁亥，彗星出天船，在胃。

translations.literal: In the second Shengping year, fifth month, day Dinghai, a comet issued from the Celestial Boat, in the Stomach.
translations.idiomatic: Shengping two, May, dinghai: a comet from Celestial Boat in the Stomach.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning, removing the old and spreading the new."
translations.idiomatic: War, death, and renewal.

translations.literal: Issuing from the Celestial Boat means outer barbarians will invade.
translations.idiomatic: From Celestial Boat marks foreign invasion.

translations.literal: One gloss says: "It will be great flood."
translations.idiomatic: A variant cites catastrophic flood.

translations.literal: In the fourth year’s fifth month, under Heaven there was great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Year four, May: realm-wide flooding.

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Emperor Mu died.
translations.idiomatic: Year five: Emperor Mu died.

sentences.zh: 哀帝興甯元年八月，有星孛於角亢，入天市。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ai’s first Xingning year, eighth month, there was a star brooming in the Horn and Neck, entering the Celestial Market.
translations.idiomatic: Xingning one, August: a broom from Horn and Neck into the Celestial Market.

translations.literal: Investigating, the prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: war and mourning.

translations.literal: In the third year’s first month, Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: Third year, first month: Empress Wang died.

translations.literal: In the second month, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: February: the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 三月，慕容恪攻沒洛陽，沈勁等戰死。

translations.literal: In the third month, Murong Ke attacked and took Luoyang; Shen Jin and others died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: March: Murong Ke took Luoyang; Shen Jin fell fighting.

sentences.zh: 海西太和四年二月，客星見紫宮西垣，至七月乃滅。

translations.literal: In Emperor Fei’s fourth Taihe year of the Haixi reign, second month, a guest star appeared on the Purple Palace’s western wall, lasting until the seventh month before it was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Haixi Taihe four, February–July: a guest star on the Purple Palace west wall.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「客星守紫宮，臣弑主。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "When a guest star guards the Purple Palace, ministers will murder the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: A guest star on the Purple Palace marks regicide.

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Huan Wen deposed the emperor as Duke of Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: Year six: Huan Wen demoted the sovereign to Duke of Haixi.

sentences.zh: 孝武甯康二年正月丁巳，有星孛於女虛，經氐、亢、角、軫、翼、張。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowu’s second Ningkang year, first month, day Dingsi, there was a star brooming in Girl and Emptiness, passing the Root, Neck, Horn, Chariot, Wings, and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Ningkang two, first month, dingsi: a broom from Girl-Void across Root, Horn, Chariot, Wings, and Zhang.

sentences.zh: 至三月丙戌，彗星，見於氐。

translations.literal: By the third month’s day Bingxu, a comet appeared in the Root.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, bingxu: a comet showed in the Root.

sentences.zh: 九月丁丑，有星孛於天市。

translations.literal: On day Dingchou in the ninth month, there was a star brooming in the Celestial Market.
translations.idiomatic: September, dingchou: a broom in the Celestial Market.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: War and mourning.

sentences.zh: 」太元元年七月，苻堅破涼州，虜張天錫。

translations.literal: In the first Taiyuan year’s seventh month, Fu Jian broke Liangzhou and captured Zhang Tianxi.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan one, July: Fu Jian conquered Liangzhou and took Zhang Tianxi.

sentences.zh: 太元十一年三月，客星在南斗，至六月乃沒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh Taiyuan year’s third month, a guest star was in the Southern Dipper, lasting until the sixth month before it sank.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan eleven, March–June: a guest star lingered in the Dipper.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "There will be arms; there will be amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: War and pardon both follow.

translations.literal: Afterward Si, Yong, Yan, and Ji constantly had military service.
translations.idiomatic: Si, Yong, Yan, and Ji then saw endless levies.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月大赦，八月又大赦。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year’s first month there was a great amnesty; in the eighth month again a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Year twelve: great pardons in first and eighth months.

sentences.zh: 十五年七月壬申，有星孛於北河戍，經太微、三台、文昌，入北斗，色白，長十餘丈。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year’s seventh month, day Renshen, there was a star brooming at the Northern River Guard, passing the Supreme Palace Enclosure, Three Steps, and Civilized Glory, entering the Northern Dipper, white in color, more than ten rods long.
translations.idiomatic: Year fifteen, July, renshen: a colossal white broom ran from the Northern River Guard through the enclosure, Three Steps, and Civilized Glory into the Dipper.

translations.literal: On day Wuxu in the eighth month, it entered the Purple Palace and then was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: August, wuxu: it entered the Purple Palace and vanished.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「北河戍一名胡門，胡有兵喪。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "The Northern River Guard is also called the Hu Gate; the Hu will have arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The Northern River Guard is the Hu Gate—steppe war and death.

sentences.zh: 掃太微，入紫微，王者當之。

translations.literal: Sweeping the Supreme Palace Enclosure and entering Purple Tenuity means the king will answer for it.
translations.idiomatic: Brushing the enclosure and Purple Tenuity hits the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 三台為三公，文昌為將相，將相三公有災。

translations.literal: The Three Steps are the Three Dukes; Civilized Glory is generals and ministers; generals and the Three Dukes will have disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Three Steps are dukes; Civilized Glory is generals—both tiers suffer.

translations.literal: Entering the Northern Dipper means feudal lords will be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the Dipper marks executed lords.

sentences.zh: 」一曰：「掃北斗，強國發兵，諸侯爭權，大人憂。

translations.literal: One gloss says: "Sweeping the Northern Dipper means a strong state will raise arms, feudal lords will contend for power, and great men will grieve."
translations.idiomatic: A variant adds hegemonic armies, baronial rivalry, and high lords’ mourning.

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty-one: the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 隆安元年，王恭、殷仲堪、桓玄等並發兵，表以誅王國寶為名。

translations.literal: In the first Long’an year, Wang Gong, Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan, and others together raised troops, memorializing in the name of executing Wang Guobao.
translations.idiomatic: Long’an one: Wang Gong, Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan, and allies mobilized to kill Wang Guobao.

sentences.zh: 朝廷順而殺之，並斬其從弟緒，司馬道子由是失勢，禍亂成矣。

translations.literal: The court yielded and killed him, also beheading his cousin Xu; Sima Daozi thereby lost power, and disaster and rebellion were accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The court complied, executed Guobao and Wang Xu, leaving Sima Daozi broken as chaos set in.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月，客星在尾中，至九月乃滅。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year’s second month, a guest star was inside the Tail, lasting until the ninth month before it was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Year eighteen, February–September: a guest star lingered in the Tail.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Yan will have arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Yan lands face war and death.

sentences.zh: 」二十年，慕容垂息寶伐魏，為所破，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Murong Chui’s son Bao campaigned against Wei and was broken by it; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty: Murong Bao attacked Wei and lost tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，垂死，國遂衰亡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Chui died, and the state then declined to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty-one: Murong Chui died and Former Yan withered.

sentences.zh: 二十年九月，有蓬星如粉絮，東南行，歷女虛，至哭星。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year’s ninth month, there was a fuzzy star like powdered floss, moving southeast, passing Girl and Emptiness, reaching the Weeping star.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty, September: a misty broom drifted southeast through Girl-Void to the Weeping star.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「蓬星見，不出三年，必有亂臣戮死於市。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "When a fuzzy star appears, within three years there must be a rebellious minister executed in the market."
translations.idiomatic: Fuzzy stars within three years bring a traitor’s public execution.

translations.literal: At the time Wang Guobao was weaving intrigues at court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao was then poisoning court politics.

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year’s ninth month, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty-one, September: the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 隆安元年，王恭等興兵，而朝廷殺王國寶、王緒。

translations.literal: In the first Long’an year, Wang Gong and others raised troops, and the court killed Wang Guobao and Wang Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Long’an one: Wang Gong’s revolt prompted the court to kill Guobao and Xu.

sentences.zh: 安帝隆安四年二月己丑，有星孛於奎，長三丈，上至閣道、紫宮西蕃，入北斗魁，至三台，三月，遂經於太微帝坐端門。

translations.literal: In Emperor An’s fourth Long’an year, second month, day Jichou, there was a star brooming in the Strider, three rods long, reaching up to the Forbidden Passage and the Purple Palace’s western bastion, entering the Dipper’s ladle, reaching the Three Steps; in the third month it then passed the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s imperial seat and Portal Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Long’an four, jichou: a three-rod broom in Kui climbed to the Forbidden Passage, crossed the Purple Palace west wall and Dipper ladle, reached Three Steps, then in March swept the enclosure throne and Portal Gate.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「彗星掃天子庭閣道，易主之象。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "When a comet sweeps the Son of Heaven’s court and Forbidden Passage, it is an image of changing the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: A comet brushing the court passage means a new sovereign.

translations.literal: It passed the Three Steps and entered the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: It crossed Three Steps into the Dipper.

translations.literal: The prognostication was the same as the entry above.
translations.idiomatic: Same gloss as the prior Three Steps–Dipper line.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊寅，有星孛于貫索、天市、天津。

translations.literal: On day Wuyin in the twelfth month, there was a star brooming in the Coiled Rope, Celestial Market, and Celestial Ford.
translations.idiomatic: December, wuyin: a broom through Coiled Rope, Market, and Ford.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「貴臣獄死，內外有兵喪。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Noble ministers die in prison; inner and outer will have arms and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: High officials perish in jail while war spreads inside and out.

sentences.zh: 天津為賊斷，王道天下不通。

translations.literal: The Celestial Ford being cut by bandits means the royal way is blocked under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ford is severed, the king’s highway is choked.

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: "The calamity lies in Wu and Yue."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary pins the sign on Wu-Yue.

sentences.zh: 」五年二月，有孫恩兵亂，攻侵郡國。

translations.literal: In the fifth year’s second month, there was Sun En’s soldier rebellion, attacking and raiding commanderies and principalities.
translations.idiomatic: Year five, February: Sun En’s mutiny ravaged the districts.

sentences.zh: 於是內外戒嚴，營陣屯守，柵斷淮口。

translations.literal: Thereupon inner and outer were placed on alert; camps and formations garrisoned and held; palisades cut off the Huai mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The realm locked down, armies walled the Huai crossings.

sentences.zh: 九月，桓玄表至，逆旨陵上。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Huan Xuan’s memorial arrived, defying the decree and lording over the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: September: Huan Xuan’s arrogant memorial snubbed the throne.

sentences.zh: 其後玄遂篡位，亂京都，大饑，人相食，百姓流亡，皆其應也。

translations.literal: Afterward Xuan then usurped the throne, threw the capital into chaos, great famine set in, men ate one another, and the hundred surnames fled—all were its responses.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan seized power, starved Jiankang into cannibalism, and drove the people—all matching the omens.

sentences.zh: 元興元年十月，有客星色白如粉絮，在太微西，至十二月入太微。

translations.literal: In the first Yuanxing year’s tenth month, there was a guest star, white like powdered floss, west of the Supreme Palace Enclosure, until the twelfth month it entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing one, October–December: a floss-white guest star slid from west of the enclosure into it.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Arms enter the Son of Heaven’s court."
translations.idiomatic: War enters the celestial court.

sentences.zh: 」二年十二月，桓玄篡位，放遷帝、后於尋陽，以永安何皇后為零陵君。

translations.literal: In the second year’s twelfth month, Huan Xuan usurped the throne, banished emperor and empress to Xunyang, and made Empress He of Yong’an the Lady of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing two, December: Huan Xuan seized the throne and exiled the sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，劉裕盡誅桓氏。

translations.literal: In the third year’s second month, Liu Yu exterminated the entire Huan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing three, February: Liu Yu wiped out the Huans.

sentences.zh: 義熙十一年五月甲申，彗星二出天市，掃帝坐，在房心北。

translations.literal: In the eleventh Yixi year, fifth month, day Jiashen, two comets issued from the Celestial Market, sweeping the imperial seat north of the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi eleven, May, jiashen: twin comets from the Market brushed the throne north of the Heart.

translations.literal: The Heart and Chamber are Song’s field allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Heart-Chamber marks Song’s celestial territory.

sentences.zh: 案占：「得彗柄者興，除舊布新，宋興之象。

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: "He who gains the comet’s handle rises; removing the old and spreading the new is an image of Song’s rise."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever catches the comet’s handle rises—an omen of Song’s founding.

sentences.zh: 」十四年五月庚子，有星孛於北斗魁中。

translations.literal: On day Gengzi in the fourteenth year’s fifth month, there was a star brooming inside the Northern Dipper’s ladle.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi fourteen, May, gengzi: a broom inside the Dipper’s ladle.

sentences.zh: 七月癸亥，彗星出太微西，柄起上相星下，芒漸長至十餘丈，進掃北斗、紫微、中台。

translations.literal: On day Guihai in the seventh month, a comet issued west of the Supreme Palace Enclosure, its handle rising below the senior minister star, its ray gradually lengthening to more than ten rods, advancing to sweep the Northern Dipper, Purple Tenuity, and the central Step.
translations.idiomatic: July, guihai: a comet sprang west of the enclosure, handle under the senior minister, tail growing ten rods to brush Dipper, Purple Tenuity, and central Step.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「彗出太微，社稷亡，天下易王；

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "When a comet exits the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the altars of soil and grain perish and under Heaven the king changes;
translations.idiomatic: A comet leaving the enclosure ends the dynasty and swaps the king;

translations.literal: entering the Northern Dipper and Purple Tenuity means the imperial palace is empty."
translations.idiomatic: piercing Dipper and Purple Tenuity empties the throne hall."

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Liu Yu returned to Pengcheng and received the title Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi fourteen: Liu Yu took the Song dukedom at Pengcheng.

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: December: the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 恭帝元年正月戊戌，有星孛於太微西蕃。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gong’s first year, first month, day Wuxu, there was a star brooming on the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s western bastion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong year one, first month, wuxu: a broom on the enclosure’s west wall.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "It is a sign of dynastic revolution."
translations.idiomatic: Marks mandate revolution.

translations.literal: That year, Song held all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Song took the realm.

translations.literal: Flowing stars and falling stars
translations.idiomatic: Shooting stars and meteor falls

sentences.zh: 蜀後主，諸葛亮帥大眾伐魏，屯于渭南。

translations.literal: Shu’s latter ruler: Zhuge Liang led a great host to campaign against Wei, encamping south of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Shu’s last king: Zhuge Liang massed an army against Wei on the Wei’s south bank.

sentences.zh: 有長星赤而芒角，自東北西南流，投亮營，三投再還，往大還小。

translations.literal: There was a long star, red with bristling rays, flowing from northeast to southwest, casting itself toward Liang’s camp, three times casting and twice returning, going large and returning small.
translations.idiomatic: A long red meteor shot southwest toward Zhuge Liang’s camp, thrice striking and twice rebounding, swelling then shrinking.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「兩軍相當，有大流星來走軍上及墜軍中者，皆破敗之徵也。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "When two armies face each other, if a great shooting star runs onto the army or falls inside the army, all are signs of defeat and destruction."
translations.idiomatic: Great meteors plunging into camps mean annihilation.

sentences.zh: 」九月，亮卒於軍，焚營而退，群帥交怨，多相誅殘。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liang died in the army; they burned the camp and withdrew; the various commanders turned on one another in blame, and many mutually slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: September: Zhuge Liang died in camp; Shu burned the lines; generals turned fratricidal.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝，宣帝圍公孫文懿于襄平。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Ming: the August Lord besieged Gongsun Wenyi at Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi: Sima Yi besieged Gongsun Yuan at Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 八月丙寅夜，有大流星長數十丈，白色有芒鬣，從首山東北流，墜襄平城東南。

translations.literal: On the night of day Bingyin in the eighth month, there was a great shooting star several tens of rods long, white with bristling mane, flowing from Shoushan northeast, falling southeast of Xiangping city.
translations.idiomatic: August, bingyin night: a huge white meteor streaked from Shoushan into Xiangping’s southeast.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「圍城而有流星來走城上及墜城中者破。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "When there is a siege and a shooting star runs onto the city or falls inside the city, it is broken."
translations.idiomatic: Meteors striking a besieged city mean its fall.

translations.literal: It also says: "Where a star falls, below it will be a battlefield."
translations.idiomatic: A second gloss sets battle where the meteor lands.

translations.literal: It also says: "In general wherever stars fall, the state changes surname."
translations.idiomatic: A third gloss ties falls to dynastic change.

sentences.zh: 」九月，文懿突圍走，至星墜所被斬，屠城，坑其眾。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wenyi broke the siege and fled; at the place the star fell he was beheaded; they slaughtered the city and buried its host in pits.
translations.idiomatic: September: Gongsun Yuan fled to the fall site and died; Xiangping was sacked and its people massacred.

sentences.zh: 元帝六月，有大流星二並如斗，見西方，分流南北，光照地，隆隆有聲。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Yuan Di’s reign, there were two great shooting stars each like a dipper-ladle, seen in the west, dividing flow south and north, their light shining on the ground, rumbling with sound.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yuan emperor’s sixth month: twin dipper-sized western meteors split north and south, lighting the earth with thunder.

sentences.zh: 案占：「流星為貴使，星大者使大。

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: "Shooting stars are noble envoys; when the star is large the envoy is great."
translations.idiomatic: Meteors image great emissaries; larger stars mean greater men.

sentences.zh: 」是年，鍾、鄧克蜀，二星蓋二帥之象。

translations.literal: That year, Zhong and Deng conquered Shu; the two stars were probably images of the two commanders.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhong Hui and Deng Ai took Shu—the twin meteors mirrored the two generals.

sentences.zh: 二帥相背，又分流南北之應。

translations.literal: The two commanders turned their backs on each other; it also matched dividing flow south and north.
translations.idiomatic: Their mutual betrayal matched the split tails.

sentences.zh: 鍾會既叛，三軍憤怒，隆隆有聲，兵將怒之徵也。

translations.literal: After Zhong Hui rebelled, the three armies were furious; rumbling with sound is a sign of soldiers and generals angry.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui mutinied, the hosts raged—the meteor’s roar imaged soldierly fury.

sentences.zh: 武帝七月，星隕如雨，皆西流。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu’s seventh month, stars fell like rain, all flowing west.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Wudi’s seventh month: a westward meteor shower.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Star falls mean the hundred surnames rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Meteor showers mean popular revolt.

translations.literal: Flowing west is an image of Wu people submitting to Jin."
translations.idiomatic: Westward flow showed Wu yielding to Jin."

sentences.zh: 」二年，吳夏口督孫秀率部曲二千餘人來降。

translations.literal: In the second year, Wu’s Xiakou commander Sun Xiu led more than two thousand households of troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Year two: Wu’s Sun Xiu brought two thousand families over.

translations.literal: On day Renzi in the eighth month, stars fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: August, renzi: another meteor rain.

translations.literal: Liu Xiang’s "Tradition" states: "It is an image of the lower displacing the upper."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang reads it as inferiors overturning superiors.

sentences.zh: 」後三年，帝崩而惠帝立，天下自此亂矣。

translations.literal: After three years the emperor died and Emperor Hui was established; under Heaven from this was chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Three years on the emperor died, Hui succeeded, and chaos engulfed the realm.

sentences.zh: 惠帝九月甲午，枉矢東北行，竟天。

translations.literal: In Emperor Hui’s ninth month, day Jiawu, a crooked arrow went northeast, spanning the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Huidi, September, jiawu: a crooked-arrow comet stretched northeast across the sky.

sentences.zh: 六年六月丙午夜，有枉矢自斗魁東南行。

translations.literal: On the night of day Bingwu in the sixth year’s sixth month, there was a crooked arrow from the Dipper’s ladle moving southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Year six, June, bingwu night: a crooked arrow left the Dipper southeastward.

translations.literal: Investigating, the prognostication states: "Using disorder to attack disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: chaos fights chaos.

sentences.zh: 北斗主執殺，出斗魁，居中執殺者，不直之象也。

translations.literal: The Northern Dipper governs executions and killing; issuing from the Dipper’s ladle, the executioner in the center not being straight is an image."
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper rules killing; a crooked arrow from its ladle marks unjust executioners."

sentences.zh: 」是後，趙王殺張、裴，廢賈后，以理太子之冤，因自篡盜，以至屠滅，以亂伐亂之應也。

translations.literal: Afterward Prince Zhao killed Zhang and Pei, deposed Empress Jia to redress the heir’s grievance, then himself usurped and stole, down to extermination—responses to using disorder to attack disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Then Sima Lun killed Zhang and Pei, toppled Empress Jia for the crown prince, then seized power and was destroyed—chaos answering chaos.

sentences.zh: 一曰，氐帥齊萬年反之應也。

translations.literal: One gloss says: it was also the response to Di chieftain Qi Wannian’s rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Another line ties the sign to Qi Wannian’s Di revolt.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛巳，有星晝隕中天北下，光變白，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On day Xinsi in the eleventh month, there was a star that fell in daytime from mid-sky to the north, its light turning white, with sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: November, xinsi: a daytime fireball dropped northward, flashed white, and thundered.

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: "Its name is Camp Head."
translations.idiomatic: The books call it a Camp Head meteor.

sentences.zh: 營首所在，下有大兵，流血。

translations.literal: Where Camp Head lies, below there will be a great army and flowing blood."
translations.idiomatic: Under Camp Head falls great slaughter."

sentences.zh: 」明年，劉元海、石勒攻略并州，多所殘滅。

translations.literal: The next year, Liu Yuan and Shi Le raided Bing Province, greatly destroying it.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Liu Yuan and Shi Le ravaged Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王浚起燕代，引鮮卑攻掠鄴中，百姓塗地。

translations.literal: Wang Jun rose in Yan and Dai, leading Xianbei to raid Ye, and the hundred surnames were smeared on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun mobilized Yan-Dai Xianbei to scour Ye and trample the people.

translations.literal: Having sound like thunder is an image of anger.
translations.idiomatic: Thunderous noise images wrath.

translations.literal: On day Yichou in the seventh month, stars fell with sound.
translations.idiomatic: July, yichou: noisy meteors.

translations.literal: In the second year’s tenth month, stars again fell with sound.
translations.idiomatic: Year two, October: more sounding meteors.

translations.literal: The prognostication was the same as above.
translations.idiomatic: Same meteor gloss.

translations.literal: Afterward, the central plain was then lost.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland was lost soon after.

translations.literal: In the fifth month, a crooked arrow flowed southwest.
translations.idiomatic: May: a crooked-arrow comet ran southwest.

sentences.zh: 是時，司馬越西破河間兵，奉迎大駕，尋收繆胤、何綏等，肆無君之心，天下惡之。

translations.literal: At the time Sima Yue broke the Hejian army in the west, welcomed the great chariot, then seized Miao Yin, He Sui, and others, wantonly showing lack of fealty to the ruler; under Heaven hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue crushed Hejian, escorted the emperor, then arrested Miao Yin and He Sui, flaunting disloyalty until the realm despised him.

sentences.zh: 及死而石勒焚其尸柩，是其應也。

translations.literal: When he died, Shi Le burned his coffin; this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le burned Yue’s bier—matching the omen.

sentences.zh: 懷帝九月辛卯，有大星如日，自西南流于東北，小者如斗，相隨，天盡赤，聲如雷。

translations.literal: In Emperor Huai’s ninth month, day Xinmao, there was a great star like the sun, flowing from southwest to northeast, small ones like dippers following, the whole sky turning red, sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Huaidi, September, xinmao: a sun-bright bolide crossed the sky with dipper-sized followers, reddening the heavens with thunder.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「流星為貴使，星大者使大。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Shooting stars are noble envoys; when the star is large the envoy is great."
translations.idiomatic: Large meteors image great agents of fate.

sentences.zh: 」是年五月，汲桑殺東燕王騰，遂據河北。

translations.literal: That year’s fifth month, Ji Sang killed Prince Teng of Eastern Yan and then held the Yellow River’s north.
translations.idiomatic: That May Ji Sang slew Prince Teng and seized north Hebei.

sentences.zh: 十一月，始遣和郁為征北將軍，鎮鄴西。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, they first dispatched He Yu as General Who Conquers the North, garrisoning west of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: November: He Yu was sent to camp west of Ye.

sentences.zh: 田甄等大破汲桑，斬于樂陵。

translations.literal: Tian Zhen and others greatly broke Ji Sang and beheaded him at Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhen shattered Ji Sang and took his head at Leling.

sentences.zh: 於是以甄為汲郡太守，弟蘭钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhen was made governor of Ji commandery and his younger brother Lan governor of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhen became Ji governor; his brother Lan Julu governor.

sentences.zh: 小星相隨者，小將別帥之象也。

translations.literal: Small stars following mean images of minor generals and separate commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Trailing small meteors mark subordinate columns.

sentences.zh: 司馬越忿魏郡以東平原以南皆党于桑，以賞甄等，於是侵掠赤地。

translations.literal: Sima Yue resented that east of Wei commandery and south of Pingyuan all sided with Sang, and rewarded Zhen and others, thereupon raiding until the land was bare.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, furious that Wei east and Pingyuan south backed Sang, rewarded Tian Zhen’s raids until the soil was scorched bare.

translations.literal: Having sound like thunder is an image of wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder again signals rage.

sentences.zh: 四年十月庚子，大星西北墜，有聲。

translations.literal: On day Gengzi in the fourth year’s tenth month, a great star fell northwest with sound.
translations.idiomatic: Year four, October, gengzi: a huge northwest meteor boomed.

translations.literal: Soon the emperor was dust-smirched at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor suffered captivity at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 元帝四月壬辰，枉矢出虛、危，沒翼、軫。

translations.literal: In Yuan Di’s fourth month, day Renchen, a crooked arrow issued from Emptiness and Rooftops and sank in Wings and Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yuan emperor, April, renchen: a crooked arrow ran Void-Rooftops to Wings-Chariot.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「枉矢所觸，天下之所伐。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "What the crooked arrow strikes is what under Heaven punishes."
translations.idiomatic: The crooked arrow marks heaven’s target.

translations.literal: Wings and Chariot are Jing Province’s field allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Wings-Chariot map to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 」，王敦殺譙王承及甘卓，而敦又梟夷，枉矢觸翼之應也。

translations.literal: Wang Dun killed Prince Cheng of Qiao and Gan Zhuo, and Dun was then executed and displayed; it was the response of the crooked arrow touching the Wings.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun slew Sima Cheng and Gan Zhuo, then died himself—the arrow’s touch on Wings fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 七月甲午，有流星大如甕，長百餘丈，青赤色，從西方來，尾分為百餘岐，或散。

translations.literal: On day Jiawu in the seventh month, there was a shooting star large as a vat, more than a hundred rods long, bluish red, coming from the west, its tail dividing into more than a hundred forks, some scattering.
translations.idiomatic: July, jiawu: a vat-sized western meteor split into a hundred tails.

sentences.zh: 時王敦之亂，百姓流亡之應也。

translations.literal: It was the response to Wang Dun’s rebellion and the hundred surnames fleeing in exile.
translations.idiomatic: It answered Wang Dun’s revolt and the people’s flight.

sentences.zh: 成帝元月辛末，流星大如二斗魁，色青赤，光耀地，出奎中，沒婁北。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng’s first month, day Xinwei, there was a shooting star large as two dipper-ladles, bluish red, its light shining on the ground, issuing from within the Strider, sinking north of Bond.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng’s first month, xinwei: a twin-dipper meteor blazed from Kui to north Bond.

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: "It is famine; the five grains are not stored."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary reads famine and empty granaries.

translations.literal: That month, great drought and famine.
translations.idiomatic: That month brought drought and hunger.

sentences.zh: 六年二月庚午朔，有流星大如斗，光耀地，出天市，西行人太微。

translations.literal: On the new moon of day Gengwu in the sixth year’s second month, there was a shooting star large as a dipper, its light shining on the ground, issuing from the Celestial Market, moving west into the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Year six, second month, gengwu new moon: a dipper-bright meteor left the Market and plunged west into the enclosure.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "A great man will answer for it."
