translations.idiomatic: A magnate bears the sign.

translations.literal: In the eighth year’s sixth month, Emperor Cheng died.
translations.idiomatic: Year eight, June: Emperor Cheng died.

sentences.zh: 穆帝六月辛巳，日未入，有流星大如三斗魁，從辰巳上，東南行。

translations.literal: In Emperor Mu’s sixth month, day Xinsi, before the sun had set, there was a shooting star large as three dipper-ladles, from above Chen and Si, moving southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Mudi, June, xinsi, before sunset: a triple-dipper meteor rose from the Chen-Si quadrant southeastward.

sentences.zh: 晷度推之，在箕、斗之間，蓋燕分也。

translations.literal: By gnomon reckoning it lay between the Sieve and Dipper, probably Yan’s division.
translations.idiomatic: Shadow reckoning placed it between Sieve and Dipper in Yan’s field.

translations.literal: Investigating the prognostication: "It is Camp Head."
translations.idiomatic: The books again call it Camp Head.

translations.literal: Below Camp Head, blood flows in torrents."
translations.idiomatic: Under Camp Head comes a blood tide."

sentences.zh: 」是時，慕容雋僭稱大燕，攻伐無已。

translations.literal: At the time Murong Jun falsely styled himself Great Yan, attacking without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun then claimed Great Yan and raided endlessly.

sentences.zh: 十年四月癸未，流星大如斗，色赤黃，出織女，沒造父，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On day Guiwei in the tenth year’s fourth month, there was a shooting star large as a dipper, red-yellow in color, issuing from the Weaving Girl, sinking in Zaofu, with sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Year ten, April, guiwei: a dipper-sized red-yellow meteor ran Weaving Girl to Zaofu with thunder.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「燕齊有兵，百姓流亡。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Yan and Qi will have arms; the hundred surnames will flee in exile."
translations.idiomatic: Yan-Qi war drives commoners into exile.

sentences.zh: 」其年十二月，慕容雋遂據臨漳，盡有幽、并、青、冀之地。

translations.literal: That year’s twelfth month, Murong Jun then occupied Linzhang and wholly held You, Bing, Qing, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: That December Murong Jun took Linzhang and held You, Bing, Qing, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 緣河諸將奔散，河津隔絕。

translations.literal: The various generals along the Yellow River scattered in flight; river fords were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: River generals fled and crossings closed.

translations.literal: Murong Ke attacked Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ke struck Qi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，枉矢自東南流於西北，其長半天。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, a crooked arrow flowed from southeast to northwest, its length half the sky.
translations.idiomatic: November: a crooked-arrow comet crossed half the sky northwestward.

sentences.zh: 四年十月庚戌，天狗見西南。

translations.literal: On day Gengxu in the fourth year’s tenth month, the Celestial Dog was seen in the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Year four, October, gengxu: the Celestial Dog appeared southwest.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "There will be great arms and flowing blood."
translations.idiomatic: Great battles and bloodshed follow.

sentences.zh: 海西十月壬申，有大流星西下，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: In Haixi’s tenth month, day Renshen, there was a great shooting star moving west down, with sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Haixi reign, October, renshen: a huge western fireball boomed.

sentences.zh: 明年，遣使免袁真為庶人。

translations.literal: The next year, an envoy was dispatched to degrade Yuan Zhen to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Next year envoys stripped Yuan Zhen of rank.

sentences.zh: 桓溫在壽春，真病死，息瑾代立，求救於苻堅。

translations.literal: Huan Wen was at Shou-chun; Zhen died of illness; his heir Jin succeeded and begged rescue from Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen held Shouyang; Yuan Zhen died and his son Jin sought Fu Jian’s aid.

translations.literal: Wen defeated Fu Jian’s army.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen broke Fu Jian’s relief column.

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Shouyang city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Year six: Shouyang fell.

sentences.zh: 孝武十月乙卯，有奔星東南經翼、軫，聲如雷。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowu’s tenth month, day Yimao, there was a racing star moving southeast through Wings and Chariot, with sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowudi, October, yimao: a bolide roared southeast through Wings and Chariot.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「楚地有兵，軍破，百姓流亡。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Chu lands will have arms; the army will be broken; the hundred surnames will flee in exile."
translations.idiomatic: Chu sees defeat, rout, and refugee columns.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，苻堅荊州刺史梁成、襄陽太守閻震率眾伐竟陵，桓石虔擊大破之，生擒震，斬首七千，獲生口萬人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Fu Jian’s Jing inspector Liang Cheng and Xiangyang defender Yan Zhen led a host to campaign against Jingling; Huan Shiqian greatly defeated them, captured Yan Zhen alive, beheaded seven thousand, and took ten thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: December: Fu Jian’s Liang Cheng and Yan Zhen struck Jingling until Huan Shiqian shattered them, taking Yan Zhen and seven thousand heads.

translations.literal: Sound like thunder is an image of generals’ anger.
translations.idiomatic: The thunder images generals’ fury.

sentences.zh: 十三年閏月戊辰，天狗東北下，有聲。

translations.literal: On day Wuchen in the thirteenth year’s intercalary month, the Celestial Dog dropped northeast with sound.
translations.idiomatic: Year thirteen, leap month, wuchen: the Celestial Dog fell northeast audibly.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "There will be a great battle and flowing blood."
translations.idiomatic: Major bloodshed follows.

sentences.zh: 」自是後，慕容垂、翟遼、姚萇、苻登、慕容永並阻兵爭強。

translations.literal: From this time Murong Chui, Zhai Liao, Yao Chang, Fu Deng, and Murong Yong all blocked roads with arms and vied for supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Murong Chui, Zhai Liao, Yao Chang, Fu Deng, and Murong Yong kept private armies.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，彭城妖賊又稱偽號於皇丘，劉牢之破滅之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year’s first month, Pengcheng’s occult bandits again falsely styled a title at Huangqiu; Liu Laozhi destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth year, first month: Pengcheng rebels styled themselves at Huangqiu until Liu Laozhi wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 三月，張道破合鄉、太山，向欽之擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhang Dao broke Hexiang and Taishan; Xiang Qinzhi drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: March: Zhang Dao hit Hexiang and Taishan until Xiang Qinzhi repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 安帝三月甲寅，流星赤色，眾多西行，經牽牛、虛、危、天津、閣道，貫太微、紫宮。

translations.literal: On day Jiayin in Emperor An’s third month, red shooting stars, numerous, moved west, passing Oxherd, Emptiness, Rooftops, Celestial Ford, Forbidden Passage, piercing the Supreme Palace Enclosure and Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An, third month, jiayin: many red meteors streamed west through key asterisms into the enclosure and Purple Palace.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「星庶人類，眾多西行，眾將西流之象。

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Stars are the likeness of commoners; numerous ones moving west are an image of many generals flowing west."
translations.idiomatic: Meteors image commoners; a western swarm means columns fleeing west.

sentences.zh: 經天子庭，主弱臣強，諸侯兵不制。

translations.literal: Passing the Son of Heaven’s court means the ruler is weak and ministers strong; feudal lords’ troops are unchecked."
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the celestial court shows a feeble throne, mighty ministers, and uncontrollable regional armies."

sentences.zh: 」其年五月，孫恩侵吳郡，殺內史。

translations.literal: That year’s fifth month, Sun En raided Wu commandery and killed the interior governor.
translations.idiomatic: That May Sun En hit Wu commandery and slew its governor.

translations.literal: In the sixth month, he reached Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: June: he reached Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 於是內外戒嚴，營陣屯守，劉裕追破之。

translations.literal: Thereupon inner and outer were placed on alert; camps and formations garrisoned and held; Liu Yu pursued and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region armed; Liu Yu chased and crushed Sun En.

sentences.zh: 元興元年七月，大饑，人相食。

translations.literal: In the first Yuanxing year’s seventh month, great famine; men ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing one, July: famine drove cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 浙江以東流亡十六七，吳郡、吳興戶口減半，又流奔而西者萬計。

translations.literal: East of the Zhe River six or seven tenths fled; Wu commandery and Wu-xing lost half their households; those who fled west also counted in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: East of Zhe six or seven in ten fled; Wu and Wu-xing halved; tens of thousands bolted west.

sentences.zh: 十月，桓玄遣將擊劉軌，破走之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Huan Xuan dispatched a general to strike Liu Gui, defeated him, and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: October: Huan Xuan’s column routed Liu Gui.

translations.literal: Gui fled to Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gui fled to Qingzhou.

translations.literal: Cloud vapors
translations.idiomatic: Anomalous cloud vapors

sentences.zh: 惠帝十二月壬寅夜，有赤氣亙天，砰隱有聲。

translations.literal: In Emperor Hui’s twelfth month, day Renyin night, there was red vapor spanning the sky, rumbling with hidden sound.
translations.idiomatic: Huidi, December, renyin night: red qi bridged the sky with low thunder.

sentences.zh: 二年十月丁丑，赤氣見北方，東西竟天。

translations.literal: In the second year’s tenth month, day Dingchou, red vapor appeared in the north, east and west spanning the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Year two, October, dingchou: northern red qi stretched horizon to horizon.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Both mean great arms."
translations.idiomatic: Both signs mean major war.

translations.literal: Rumbling with hidden sound is an image of anger.
translations.idiomatic: The rumble images wrath.

translations.literal: Afterward the four seas were cloud-turbulent and the nine domains crossed arms.
translations.idiomatic: Then the realm boiled in war on every border.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲申，有白氣若虹，中天北下至地，夜見五日乃滅。

translations.literal: On day Jiashen in the twelfth month, there was white vapor like a rainbow, from mid-sky north down to the ground, seen five nights then extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: December, jiashen: white arc from zenith to earth lasted five nights.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Great arms will arise."
translations.idiomatic: Major war follows.

sentences.zh: 」明年，王彌起青徐，汲桑亂河北，毒流天下。

translations.literal: The next year, Wang Mi rose in Qing and Xu, Ji Sang threw Hebei into chaos, and poison spread under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Wang Mi and Ji Sang’s risings poisoned the realm.

sentences.zh: 懷帝十一月乙亥，有白氣如帶，出南北方各二，起地至天，貫參伐中。

translations.literal: In Emperor Huai’s eleventh month, day Yihai, there was white vapor like a belt, two each issuing south and north from ground to sky, piercing Orion’s Belt and the伐 stars.
translations.idiomatic: Huaidi, November, yihai: paired white belts crossed Orion’s Blade.

translations.literal: The prognostication states: "Under Heaven great arms will arise."
translations.idiomatic: Realm-wide war is portended.

translations.literal: In the fourth year’s third month, Sima Yue arrested Miao Yin and others.
translations.idiomatic: Year four, March: Sima Yue seized Miao Yin and company.

translations.literal: Moreover, the three fronts were cloud-turbulent, attacking without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Three war zones seethed without pause.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，司馬越死于甯平城，石勒攻破其眾，死者十餘萬人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year’s third month, Sima Yue died at Ningping; Shi Le broke his host; the dead exceeded one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Year five, March: Yue died at Ningping; Shi Le annihilated his army, killing over a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 六月，京都焚滅，帝如虜庭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the capital was burned out; the emperor went to the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: June: Luoyang burned and the emperor fell captive.

sentences.zh: 愍帝十月己巳夜，有赤氣曜於西北。

translations.literal: In Emperor Min’s tenth month, day Jisi night, red vapor blazed in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Mindi, October, jisi night: red qi flared northwest.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史陶侃討杜弢之党於石城，戰敗。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province Tao Kan campaigned against Du Tao’s faction at Stone City and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jing inspector Tao Kan attacked Du Tao’s allies at Stone City and lost.
